Subject: Indemnity carveouts + evidence list (Order Form redlines attached)

Hi Naomi —

Thanks for the walkthrough earlier. Procurement and our GC asked me to follow up with formal redlines to the Order Form focused on indemnity for IP infringement and third-party claims.

High-level asks from our side:
- Limit Redwood's obligation to defend/reimburse to direct damages and cap exposure tied to annual spend (we suggested 1x ARR)
- Carve out open-source or third-party data training claims from your indemnity scope
- Require a documented evidence package and a contact point for technical verification if a claim arises

I attached Nebula_Redlines_OrderForm_v3.pdf with highlighted sections. GC would like an explicit list of what evidence we will be asked to provide (logs, input samples, call traces, model hashes, etc.) and SLA for Redwood to acknowledge and start triage.

We also need to confirm whether you can accept defense control (Redwood defends) or whether Nebula must retain the right to step in if Redwood chooses counsel that conflicts with our interests.

Goal: procurement review next Wed. Please let me know if you need more context.

Thanks —
Jason
Director, Procurement
Nebula Health

Attachments: Nebula_Redlines_OrderForm_v3.pdf

From: Naomi Feldman <naomi_feldman@redwood.ai>

Cc: Kim Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-19T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Indemnity carveouts + evidence list (Order Form redlines attached)

Jason —

Appreciate the clear framing and the redlines. We're not able to accept an uncapped IP indemnity tied only to ARR. That said, we can propose a commercial compromise and an operational evidence workflow that balances both sides. Summary of Redwood's proposal below: 

1) Liability cap: mutual cap equal to 1x the annual fees for the relevant Order Form (subject to a higher exception for willful misconduct).
2) Defense control: Redwood will have the right to defend third-party IP claims, but Nebula may appoint separate counsel at its own cost if there is a conflict of interest; both sides must cooperate and share information.
3) Evidence & triage: we can accept the suggested evidence types. We'll need:
   - Initial notice + representative samples of the allegedly infringing output
   - Input timestamped logs (48–72 hour window around the event)
   - Model and deployment identifiers (model name, version, quantization profile)
   - Callback traces / API request IDs to reproduce the example within a Redwood sandbox request replay
   - Signed custodian statement from Nebula's security/engineering contact confirming provenance of the inputs
4) Timeline: Redwood acknowledges claims within 3 business days; initial triage update w/in 10 business days; target remediation plan w/in 30 business days or earlier if a production outage exists.
5) Insurance / escrow: For larger deals, we can agree to an insurance-backed cap (Redwood to provide evidence of insurance) or special escrow arrangements for IP claims exceeding a threshold (suggested threshold: $250k).

I attached a short counter with suggested language for the Order Form (Redwood_Indemnity_Counter_v1.docx) and a technical-evidence-template link in case your ops/procurement team wants a checklist.

If Nebula can accept a mutual 1x-fees cap and the timeline above we can prepare a redline by EOD tomorrow for procurement. If procurement insists on an uncapped IP obligation, we will need to escalate for an insurance/escrow solution plus additional commercial concessions.

Thoughts?

—Naomi
Sr. Counsel, Contracts & Compliance
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood_Indemnity_Counter_v1.docx

Naomi —

Thanks for the clear proposal. Two quick clarifications so I can present to our CFO and GC:
- The mutual cap at "1x annual fees" — does that use the most recent 12 months or the annual committed spend on the Order Form? Procurement prefers committed spend.
- On defense control: GC wants explicit language allowing Nebula to assume defense if Redwood fails to defend diligently. Can you add a 30-day cure period to the clause?

Also: can you share a concrete sample indemnity clause (plain-text) and the technical evidence template so I can attach those to the procurement memo? Their checklist requires an evidence template.

If we can get your final redline by tomorrow EOD, procurement will aim to approve next Wed as planned.

Appreciate the flexibility —
Jason

Jason / team —

Draft clause snippet below that we believe addresses both sides' operational needs. Feel free to paste into your redline. I can also produce a tracked-change version on the Order Form if you prefer.

--- begin snippet ---
"Subject to the limitation of liability set forth in this Order Form, each party ("Indemnifying Party") shall indemnify, defend and hold harmless the other party ("Indemnified Party") from and against any third-party claim to the extent arising out of alleged infringement of a third party's intellectual property rights by the Indemnifying Party's deliverables. The Indemnifying Party shall assume control of the defense and settlement of such claim, provided that the Indemnified Party may, at its election and expense, assume control of the defense if the Indemnifying Party fails to commence defense within thirty (30) days of written notice or if a conflict of interest exists. The parties shall cooperate and exchange information necessary to the defense.

For clarity, "third-party claim" excludes claims arising solely from: (i) Customer's modification of the deliverable; (ii) Customer-provided inputs that are unlawful or infringing; or (iii) outputs that are solely a transformation of Customer-provided copyrighted material.

The aggregate liability for IP indemnity claims shall be limited to the greater of (i) the amount of fees paid by the Customer to Redwood under the applicable Order Form in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim; or (ii) $250,000.
"--- end snippet ---

Operational notes: include a "notice packet" requirement that lists the evidence items Naomi outlined. Our suggested SLA language for acknowledgements and triage timelines is reasonable and gives ops a playbook.

Naomi — if that snippet looks good I can put it into the doc and send a tracked redline by noon. Ben — if procurement wants a commercial concession we'll need specifics so we can align with finance.

Kim
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
